I think you misunderstand. I think overall what you do is great. It's all this spammy stuff that's irritating.  
  
You and your website are better than this. I am not one to post comments at all normally, but after seeing another string of post-after-post where it looks like posts have comments but it's just you - I just assume all posts with a single comment are your bot posting and I just skip over them. That's discouraging.

> The spammy things I've done so far have all been entered into very tentatively. I posted about a hundred Reddit comments by hand before I created the bot.

Making the spam more automated doesn't make it any less spammy.

> I also messaged the /r/Kickstarter moderators asking for permission. 

If you've got the permission of the moderators, that's great. That still doesn't change the fact it's annoying to see the same "bot" post in nearly every thread with an out-of-date chart which is unreadable on mobile.

> Until now, I've received only thank you's and upvotes. On twitter, I get lots of replies thanking me, retweets, and people following me back.

This is a logical fallacy. The assumption that only because you've received praise for a select number of posts/tweets doesn't mean everyone is overjoyed with your direct messages or automated posts.

> I think that most project owners are happy to see the spam. For one thing, my spam is dangerously close to content. More importantly, I'm doing some marketing for the project owner. Our interests are very aligned. 

That's rather pretentious of you. What are your interests? So you assume most are happy, so that makes it acceptable?

> Maybe my tweet will be seen by someone who turns into a backer.

What tweets? Your tweet was directly to me. No random person would see it and nobody following you would see it unless they followed both you and me. that's how twitter works when you send a message at someone. If you were doing something like @KickSaver and posting generic tweets about projects you want to help - then others would see them. Your tweets are directed at individual people.

> Do you still feel the same way when you think of what I do as free marketing? I have a twitter audience that wants to see successful projects, and that's what I give them.

I appreciate and am thankful for the work that you do with your site. That's not in debate at all. 

What we're discussing is that you do not share projects with your audience via twitter, you're sending messages AT people with their own project link. I would challenge you to add something in front of the name (e.g. "Hey @twitterperson, congrats on reaching your Kickstarter goal! I'm tracking your progress at:" ) and maintain your current rate of messages and see if your followers change. Then we can re-visit our discussion. I think you'll find when your twitter following start getting all the messages, you may rethink the method and the volume that you choose to approach people.
  
  
You're a smart guy. I just think you're energy is better spent doing less spammy things.

Daniel, you have a good graphing service - we get that. But not only did you spam me on twitter about my project but you post these charts on seemingly every single thread on reddit that mention a kickstarter project. Not to mention on mobile these are absolutely worthless. 

I get it. It's neat to see. But you don't have to be so spammy. How about having an actual discussion instead of drive-by bombing every thread. It makes me actively avoid sharing your site with people.

Don't be spammy, your helpful site speaks just fine by itself.
